dash.subtitle: This Rite instance at a glance

admin.zkBody: The server never sees a key. Collection names are readable here only through the Admin-group escrow, and machine credentials stay sealed to members. Collections created before the escrow existed appear by id until re-keyed. Available here: decrypt names, remove a member, delete a collection, grant a member access to the name and roster. Full machine access still needs a member to seal the item key.

coll.title: Collection governance
coll.subtitle: Policies and oversight, server-wide
coll.allowCreateNote: When off, only admins provision collections.
coll.allowSharingNote: Members can add anyone in the directory, not just teammates.
coll.defaultRoleNote: Applied when someone is added to a collection.
coll.confirmDelete: Force-delete this collection for every member? Its encrypted machines are lost.
coll.grantTitle: Grant access to the name and roster
coll.grantNote: Adds the user to the roster and lets them see the collection name.
coll.grantUnavailable: Available once the collection is escrowed to the Admin group (created after the escrow, or re-keyed).
coll.noSharedPersonal: No shared collections — the personal ones stay private.

inst.bindsClient: This binds the client, not the data.
inst.title: Instance
inst.lead: A name for this server, shown on the sign-in screen and in the header.
inst.saved: Saved. It shows after everyone's next reload.
inst.hostKeyShare: To be shared, so users can pin this server on first connect.
inst.persistence: Keep users signed in across reloads
inst.persistenceDesc: Each vault key sits in that browser's session storage and is cleared when the tab closes; it never leaves the browser. Off: a RAM-only key, so a reload means a re-login.
inst.openRegDesc: On, the sign-in screen offers “Create an account”: anyone who can reach this server registers themselves, as a plain user with no team. Leave off for an invite-only instance.
inst.allowInvDesc: Off closes the enrollment-token path instance-wide: no new tokens, and existing ones stop working. Independent of open registration.
inst.confirmRoleDesc: On, changing a role in Users asks first — a guard against an accidental promotion. A prompt, applied on every client.
inst.capsDesc: What connected clients may do on this server.
inst.shellOpensChoice: What a member gets until they choose otherwise.
inst.shellOpensFixed: Every terminal, for everyone — web-UI members do not pick their own.
inst.shellPrefix: The shell a terminal here opens.
inst.shellDesktop: Desktop users run their own machine's shell. Installed here:
inst.shellChoiceDesc: The default above is then the only shell. On, a member picks among the installed shells in “Settings ▸ Terminals”, and one terminal at a time from the + beside the tabs. They choose a name, never a path.
inst.quickSshDesc: Ad-hoc one-off SSH from the toolbar. Connections on a server belong in collections, saved and auditable. On for teams that need throwaway sessions.
inst.hostKeyModeDesc: One policy for everyone, since every connection runs here. Strict refuses a host key it has not seen; warn and accept do not, so neither would refuse a man-in-the-middle either. Clients show it read-only.
inst.storedSecretsDesc: What may rest in a member's own vault, and whether they can read it back.
inst.secretStorageWhat: An SSH password, a key passphrase, a key carried in the record.
inst.secretStorageDefault: Each member's own box starts unticked. Off: nothing is written and each is asked at every connection.
inst.secretStorageBinds: A record is sealed before it reaches this instance.
inst.secretReveal: Members may read a stored secret back
inst.secretRevealWhen: On an explicit action, and never on screen by itself. Off: the vault is write-only here.
inst.secretRevealBinds: A browser decrypts the record it connects with, so the boundary that holds is who the collection is shared with.
inst.hcDesc: comes from users' own connections and costs nothing.
inst.hcActiveDesc: makes requests from every client — a scan-like footprint at scale — so it is governed here.
inst.showStatusDesc: The passive “last seen” pastille. No probing.
inst.probeLegend: Off is passive only · On-demand probes when a user asks · Full allows background polling · Client's choice lets each client pick its cadence.
inst.methodsDesc: ICMP is blocked on some networks and required on others. Clients may use only a method enabled here.
inst.whoProbesDesc: Empty means everyone. Add usernames to restrict active probing; passive “last seen” stays available to all.
inst.minIntervalDesc: Floor for background polling, so status never saturates the network.
inst.dashDesc: These two cards run a command on the host each time they refresh. The rest of the dashboard reads what Rite already holds.
inst.dashStrength: The two are not equally strong. Web UI is enforcement: this server runs the commands, so off means nothing runs. Clients is policy: a client probes from its own network and this server never sees it — the official client hides the cards, a modified one could ignore the switch.
inst.dashWebuiDesc: This server runs the commands, so its own egress pays. Off is off for everyone in a browser.
inst.dashWebuiLabel: Allow the dashboard probing cards in the web UI
inst.dashClientsDesc: Each client probes from its own network, so the endpoints pay. A user may also turn the cards off locally; neither side overrides the other upward.
inst.dashClientsLabel: Allow the dashboard probing cards in attached clients
inst.dashIntervalDesc: Floor between automatic refreshes. Clients apply a floor of their own, so a very small number buys little. Pressing Refresh is not limited, and a dashboard nobody watches does not poll.
inst.managedBy: Set by this instance's configuration ({origin}) — change it there, not here.
